title: Large Attachment
summary: Checks attachments against each service's real size limit, counting email's Base64 overhead, so a message doesn't bounce for being too big.
description: Attachment size check against each service's limit, counting email's ~37% Base64 overhead, that marks the fewest files pushing it over and shows the size after sending them as a link or compressing, with an honest estimate for already-compressed files.
catches: Total over the service limit once Base64 encoding is counted
The fewest (largest-first) files to remove so the rest fits
Size after sending culprits as a link
Compression that won't help already-compressed files
limits: Built-in limits (Gmail 25 MB, Outlook.com 20 MB, Discord free 10 MB) can change and differ for workplace accounts; pass your own
The recipient's server may have a lower limit than the sender's
a11y: Service picker is a labelled radiogroup with roving tabindex and arrow keys
Status is a polite live region
Attachment list is a labelled list; icons are aria-hidden
stops: Email bounced for a big attachment
